items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: There was a young man living in Oxford who became quite friendly with the musicians... Theodore came back stage with all the money that had been taken in... We divided the money in equal part

ctx.x: Freddie Jenkins fingered the trumpet with his left hand because he had lost the joints of the upper part of the digits on his right hand.

Carpenter started showing me different things concerning phrases on the trumpet and I've always considered him my first teacher although he was not teaching me to read music. Theodore had travelled with many carnival shows and told me many things about the places he had been. His mother lived in Cincy and at the time when I met him, he was living on Richmond Street which was not far from where I had lived with Aunt Mary. It was on the corner of Richmond Street and Mound Streets that I used to go get beer for my…

It was at Carpenter's house that I heard my first Victor record. It was by a trumpet-player named Johnny Dunn and the side I remember was a blues called "I've Been Down So Long". The second line was: "Until down don't worry me".
